<xpln lang="en">See METHINKS and
MESEEMS. I thought; it appeared to me. I know not
that any author has meseemed, though it is more grammati­
cal, and deduced analogically from meseems.
<term lang="quo">Methought, a serpent eat my heart away,
And you sat similing at his cruel prey. Shakespeare.</term>
<term lang="quo">Since I sought
By pray'r th'offended deity t' appease;
Kneel'd, and before him humbl'd all my heart.
Methought, I saw him placable, and mild,
Bending his ear: persuasion in me grew
That I was heard with favour; peace return'd
Home to my breast; and to my memory
His promise, "That thy seed shall bruise our foe." Milt.</term>
<term lang="quo">In these
I found not what, methought, I wanted still. Milton.</term>
<term lang="quo">Methought I stood on a wide river's bank,
Which I must needs o'erpass, but knew not how. Dryden.</term></xpln>
